prompt: A bus holds at most $40$ students. $12$ students are already aboard, and the rest arrive in groups of $4$. Using $12 + 4g \le 40$, what is the greatest number of whole groups $g$ that can still board? Give just the number.
hint: Subtract the $12$ students already aboard from both sides.

hints.text: Subtract the $12$ students already aboard from both sides.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a smaller bus: if it holds $20$ and $12$ are aboard, only $8$ seats remain. Find the leftover seats first, then split them into groups.
$g \le 7$, so at most $7$ groups can board.

explanation: The greatest whole number of groups is 7. Check: $12 + 4(7) = 40$ students — exactly full, and "at most 40" allows it. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the empty seats
steps: Each group fills 4 seats, so $28 \div 4 = 7$ groups fit exactly.
An 8th group would need 4 more seats than the bus has.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: 40 ÷ 4 = 10 groups forgets the 12 students already in their seats.
Seats left: 40 − 12 = 28. Then 28 ÷ 4 = 7 groups. Subtract what is used before dividing what is left.
